subject: SLO measurement flapping and evidence plan / temporary carveout request
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novafin.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: infra@novafin.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Intermittent p95 spikes — request for temporary measurement carveout

Hi Nikhil,

We’ve been tracking a string of p95 latency spikes for our Hosted API traffic over the last 10 days. Our SLO in the contract is p50 120ms / p95 450ms measured on a 24h sliding window, but spikes (mostly around 02:00–04:00 UTC) are causing repeat breach notices in our internal observability tooling.

Before we escalate to procurement, can Redwood confirm whether these are measurement artifacts (sampling / aggregation) or genuine degradation? If needed, Novafin would like to request a short, targeted carveout for the region/epoch while we collect traces — we can supply request IDs and sample payloads.

Attaching a quick CSV of ~2k request ids where we observed the spike (novafin_latency_samples.csv).

Thanks,
— Elena
Senior Platform Engineer, Novafin
[Attachment: novafin_latency_samples.csv (csv)]

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novafin.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p95 spikes — request for temporary measurement carveout

Elena — thanks for the sample set and the heads up. Putting the short answer up front: we’re happy to coordinate a short carveout if evidence points to a measurement window artifact (e.g., dayparted traffic blasts compressing the p95 calc). If it’s true-system latency, we’ll need a remediation plan before we agree to a contractual adjustment.

Plan proposal:
- We’ll ingest your sample ids and cross-reference with our trace archive (I’ve asked infra to dump the matching traces).
- Run a deterministic replay on a reserved Dedicated patch to check whether tail latencies reproduce off-hosted infra.
- While we investigate (target 72 business hours), we can provisionally exclude the UTC 02:00–04:00 epoch for the p95 rolling window if both sides agree on the evidence bundle.

Can you confirm the time zone of the samples (are they in UTC?) and whether the traffic pattern for those IDs is predominantly batched background jobs? Also: please share any PagerDuty alerts or internal SLO thresholds that are firing — it helps to match alert boundaries.

I’ve attached a short runbook we’ll follow for the evidence collection and a draft evidence checklist.

— Nikhil
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: runbook-hosted-api.md (md)]

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novafin.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: infra@novafin.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 02:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Intermittent p95 spikes — request for temporary measurement carveout

Nikhil — thanks, we confirmed timestamps are UTC. The traffic is a mix: roughly 60% customer-facing interactive calls, 40% scheduled batch enrichment. The attached CSV includes a "batch_flag" column.

PagerDuty alert: "NOV-SLO-P95-ALARM" fired 11x across last 7 days, mostly between 02:10–03:30 UTC. We’ll drop a consolidated PagerDuty export into your drive link.

We agree to the 72-business-hour investigation window and provisional epoch exclusion if the traces show aggregation artifacts. Please treat this as time-sensitive — our product team is pausing a rollout until we get clarity.

Best,
Elena
[Attachment: novafin_pagerduty_export_20261110.csv (csv)]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com, Elena Torres <elena.torres@novafin.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:33:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p95 spikes — request for temporary measurement carveout

Elena / Nikhil — quick update from our diagnostics: the infra team replayed the sample set against a dedicated instance and reproduced the tail behavior, but the root cause looks like two compounding factors:

1) Batched job bursts that create head-of-line blocking at the batching service boundary (these increase variance for short intervals).
2) Our rolling-window implementation currently uses a 24h sliding window without a daypart-aware smoothing step; the p95 can spike during localized bursts and then pull the metric up for the remainder of the window until it ages out.

Proposed remedy and temporary terms:
- Immediate: provisional p95 carveout for the UTC 02:00–04:00 epoch for seven days while Novafin and Redwood validate mitigation (we will exclude those two hours from p95 calculation but still report the raw metric to your dashboard).
- Evidence bundle: we’ll provide trace exports, a deterministic replay log, and a short whitepaper describing the batching artifact (see attached slo-evidence-summary.pdf).
- Mitigation: Redwood will propose a change to the measurement pipeline (daypart smoothing) in 2 weeks and provide a rollout plan including test-canary.

Conditions:
- This carveout is provisional and limited to the specified epoch and seven-day duration. If additional high-severity failures occur during the window unrelated to the batching artifact, Redwood reserves the right to withdraw the carveout.
- We’ll add a clause to the contractual SLO amendment specifying the temporary carveout and the evidence package required for any future requests.

Ben — can you prepare the short amendment draft (one paragraph) and a HubSpot task for legal review?

— Laura
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo-evidence-summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novafin.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:47:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p95 spikes — request for temporary measurement carveout

Elena — confirming next steps and finalizing the carveout: we’ve provisionally applied the UTC 02:00–04:00 epoch exclusion to your p95 reporting window effective 2026-11-18T00:00:00Z for seven calendar days. During this period we will:

- Deliver the full evidence bundle to your Drive link (trace export, replay logs, runbook validation) — link sent to your infra contact.
- Create the one-paragraph SLO amendment and open HS-94211 for legal review (Ben to own).
- Schedule a 30-minute technical sync for 2026-11-20 to review the daypart smoothing design and pilot plan.

If Novafin confirms this aligns to your needs, we’ll close the carveout ticket and attach the amendment to the contract as a limited-time addendum. If your team wants a longer window, please provide the justification in the next 48 hours and we’ll escalate to Sales Ops.

Thanks for moving fast on the evidence — appreciate the collaboration.

— Nikhil
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: runbook-hosted-api.md (md), slo-evidence-summary.pdf (pdf), novafin_latency_samples.csv (csv)]
